posts.author: geso
posts.content_md:
Hey Justin,

Coincidental, but just the other day a friend of mine from work gave me a 46" DLP tv. He bought a plasma tv and didn't want this anymore. So I sacrificed it in the name of science 

This Panasonic tv worked perfectly for digital inputs (HDMI, PC, etc..) BUT, the analog RF input gave a distorted picture. My friend searched the internet and found this particular tv had this problem. Works fine if you have digital cable, or want to hook it up to your pc, but otherwise it would cost too much $$ to fix.

Besides having a very large 46" x 30" front surface mirror, the great thing about this was all the components inside were modular. Ie. the power supply, DLP chip/projector lamp/color wheel, and video boards were separate. I'm going to try and incorporate some parts into a smaller working unit. I was really excited about this once I started taking the tv apart, since all these parts were really much smaller than I though they'd be! 

I'm going to remove the projector lamp, color wheel, and optics assembly so I can use the DLP assembly module by itself. The DLP module has a video processor board that I 'think' can be run without the other video boards, using the DVI video plug. The DLP module also controls the color wheel which I am going to remove. Worst case scenario is I'll have to use the separate video board, but that would be fine.

I plan on taking some pictures which will make an explanation much easier. I'll post a link on this thread to the pics if anyone is interested. 

Conclusion:

I encourage any holographer looking to experiment w/ DLP, or who is looking for large FS mirrors, to get one of these tv's.

I'd search craigslist for broken DLP tv's. Say you'll pick it up and I bet it'll be free. The tv I took apart only needed a phillips head screwdriver. It took me 20 minutes to have separated the excellent electronics, pile of plastic, and the big mirror. All the plastic was nicely separated, cracked apart, and put in my recycle bin which was picked up today.

This can also be done quickly and discretly without the wife/girlfriend knowing that you've accumulated more stuff! LOL 

-George

posts.author: LarryD
posts.content_md:
> **geso:** The DLP module also controls the color wheel which I am going to remove. Worst case scenario is I'll have to use the separate video board, but that would be fine.

geso- If the TV has a color wheel, then there will be some form of feedback to sync up with the output buffers. I did this with a Proxima DLP projector. The unit wouldn't even try to put out an image (flashed error codes on the LED front panel display) without knowing the position of the color wheel. This is needed to output the correct R/G/B frame. Actually my color wheel was R/G/R/B. To get around this sync issue I probed what I could tell was the optical feedback sensor with a scope and noted the waveform, which happened to just be a short duty-cycle square wave. Then I used a 555 timer circuit to reproduce that waveform (close enough.) Again, since this signal is syncing the output buffers you don't need super tight accuracy. I used a pot to set the 555's freq. and just cranked it up until the error codes went away.

One more problem was that the HV supply for the lamp, which also had feedback to the controller. This feedback was via an opto-isolator which I cut out and just strapped the input to the controller to +5 and to GND to see what level meant "HV OK" I'd suspect there may also be other interlock/feedback schemes used. Try to get a schematic for.

BTW Is that mirror a flat one?

What model was this TV?

Larry

posts.author: geso
posts.content_md:
Hi Larry,

Thanks for the info! Since I threw away all the identifying stickers I can only guess this TV is a Samsung HLP5063W, as some of the parts indicated they were for this particular tv. Also searching the model number gave the problem associated with this tv.

The color wheel on mine is B/R/G/B/R/G then a 100% reflective mirror. On the color wheel I see IR sensor and black 'blanking patch.' I have a 555 square wave generator I made for a clock signal for another project, so I'll just use that to trick the controller.

I'm just starting to remove all the components, so will let you know how things progress. I found one interesting thing, an electronically controlled mirror. 

[http://www.hysonic.com/eng/products_SP_Actuator01.asp](http://www.hysonic.com/eng/products_SP_Actuator01.asp)

I also will look at the feedback from the HV supply to the controller. On mine its a 4 wire cable, plugged into the controller directly next to the feedback wires from the color wheel.

The mirror from the tv is just a large flat FS mirror.

-George
